{
  "research_question": "Does stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) significantly affect mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the fixed factor.",
    "For 'Success', since the data is binary (0/1), perform a Chi-square test of independence or a logistic regression ANOVA (GLM with binomial family) instead of standard ANOVA, as normality assumptions will be violated.",
    "For 'Time-to-Target', 'Path Efficiency', 'Average Speed', and 'AD', proceed with standard one-way ANOVA if normality and homogeneity of variance assumptions are met.",
    "If omnibus F-tests are significant, proceed to post-hoc pairwise comparisons."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check for normality of residuals for continuous variables (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) using Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests; note that 'Time-to-Target' has a highly skewed distribution (min=0.5, max=201.39, mean=2.80, sd=2.08), suggesting a potential need for log-transformation or non-parametric alternatives (Kruskal-Wallis).",
    "Check for homogeneity of variances (homoscedasticity) across the five groups using Levene's test or Bartlett's test.",
    "Inspect residuals for independence and lack of pattern.",
    "For 'Success', verify expected cell counts for Chi-square assumptions or use binomial GLM diagnostics."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If the omnibus ANOVA F-test is significant for a continuous variable, conduct Tukey's HSD (Honestly Significant Difference) test for all pairwise comparisons between the five paradigms.",
    "If the omnibus test for 'Success' (via Chi-square or GLM) is significant, conduct pairwise comparisons using Bonferroni-corrected z-tests or post-hoc contrasts from the logistic model.",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., eta-squared for ANOVA, Cramer's V for Chi-square) for significant findings."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Based on summary statistics, 'Sham' is expected to show significantly worse performance (lower Success, higher Time-to-Target, lower Path Efficiency, lower Average Speed, lower AD) compared to all other paradigms.",
    "The 'Combined' paradigm is expected to yield the highest Success rate and likely the best Path Efficiency and Average Speed.",
    "Significant differences in 'Time-to-Target' are expected, with 'Sham' having the highest mean (4.68) compared to others (ranging 2.56-3.14).",
    "Significant differences in 'AD' are expected, with 'Sham' showing the lowest dispersion (0.236) compared to 'Combined' (0.399), though the interpretation of 'lower is better' vs 'higher is better' for AD requires domain context; however, the difference is statistically likely given the spread."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The 'Time-to-Target' variable exhibits strong right-skewness (max 201.39 vs mean 2.80), violating the normality assumption of standard ANOVA; a transformation or non-parametric test may be required.",
    "The 'Success' variable is binary, making standard ANOVA inappropriate without adjustment.",
    "Unequal sample sizes across paradigms (n=3323 to n=48846) may affect the power and robustness of the tests, though ANOVA is generally robust to moderate imbalance.",
    "The dataset represents a single replication (Replication: 1), limiting the ability to generalize findings across different experimental runs or temporal variations."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct a one-way ANOVA on log-transformed 'Time-to-Target' and 'Path Efficiency' (if skewed), and a Chi-square test or Binomial GLM for 'Success', followed by Tukey's HSD or Bonferroni-corrected pairwise comparisons for significant omnibus results."
}
